families.rationale: Face views show two independently recorded six-arm stars at 28, 30 and 32 degree relative rotations, producing twelve distinguishable branches; start, middle and final captures show continuous component growth with clear viewport margins.
Oblique and axial views show six tapered bullet components radiating from one center; the 48, 52 and 56 degree polar tilts give a controlled trio while retaining separated radial axes.
Six plate components form a radial three-dimensional plate cluster in every slot, and the 36, 40 and 44 degree polar tilts visibly vary the fan without changing the accepted component source.
Six branched dendritic components remain recognizable in the three review views and form a radial spatial cluster; 44, 48 and 52 degree polar tilts provide the registered small variation.

Oblique and axial views show three capped-column growth records arranged along one long axis, with repeated caps visible and ample vertical clearance; spacing values 0.9, 1.0 and 1.1 distinguish the trio.
Two separate solid-column components are visible in oblique and axial review, and the 8, 10 and 12 degree opening angles produce a controlled twin-column variation without overlap or clipping.

Six reproducible components with explicit unequal positions, orientations and scales form a visibly irregular three-dimensional aggregate; scale spreads 0.08, 0.10 and 0.12 change only the registered driver.
The corrected polar-axis transforms produce six distinct slender needle directions around a common center in oblique review; 40, 44 and 48 degree tilts preserve the cluster while varying its opening.
Two branched components meet as a symmetric wing-like arrowhead pair, with face and oblique views confirming the twin construction; 54, 58 and 62 degree openings provide the registered trio.
Face review clearly shows two long needle components crossing on distinct axes rather than overlapping; the measured 86, 90 and 94 degree recipes visibly bracket a right-angle cross.
Oblique and axial views separate two intersecting plate components, while 56, 60 and 64 degree crossing angles form a controlled three-scene range with complete growth progression and clearance.
